title: Free DC!
author: Bruce Altschuler
content:
On August 11, 2025, Donald Trump ordered the Secretary of Defense to mobilize
the D.C. National Guard to combat what [he claimed
](https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-lede/can-donald-trump-police-the-united-
states)was “an epidemic of crime in our Nation’s capital,” even though earlier
that year, the D.C. United States Attorney’s office had announced that crime
there was at a 30-year low.

According to the Metropolitan Police Department, violent crime in the city had
[declined by 26%](https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/is-dc-crime-
totally-out-of-control-as-trump-said-what-the-numbers-show/3972118/) during
the previous year. Although the Supreme Court upheld a lower court decision
holding that the President lacked the authority to deploy National Guard
troops in Chicago over the objections of the state’s governor, D.C. is
different because, unlike states, it does not have a governor in charge of the
state’s National Guard. Instead, the President has control.

The basic rule in the United States is that unlike the leaders of countries
that employ the military as an instrument of domestic control, the President
cannot use it as a police force. According to the Supreme Court in _[Laird v.
Tatum (1972)](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/408/1/)_ , there is
“a traditional and strong resistance of Americans to any military intrusion
into civilian affairs” that has “deep roots in our history.”

Passed in 1878, the [Posse Comitatus Act](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-
work/research-reports/posse-comitatus-act-explained) forbids the military from
enforcing laws within the United States without express congressional or
constitutional authority. However, because Donald Trump is essentially the
governor of Washington DC, unlike the rest of the country, it is exempt from
the Act.

The unique status of DC means that Congress has the final say over its
governance. Until the [1973 Home Rule Act](https://dccouncil.gov/dc-home-
rule/), federally appointed commissioners and Congress, none of whom were
elected by the city’s residents, controlled the laws and budget. That law,
while not giving local citizens the opportunity to elect members of Congress,
did allow them to elect a government to run the district’s day-to-day affairs
although Congress retained the power to overrule that government’s decisions.

Because soldiers are not trained in law enforcement, the duties of the
National Guard troops in DC, according to the Defense department, are
“administrative and logistical support,” as well as “providing a physical
presence in support of law enforcement.” They cannot make arrests, carry out
searches, or investigate crimes-but they have been used to visibly patrol the
streets and even temporarily detain people until the police arrive. This
sounds to many like intimidation, especially of protesters and the most
vulnerable. If it leads to violence, that could provide an excuse for a
crackdown.

In essence, the National Guard troops have roamed the streets like an
occupying army for nearly a year despite the fact that the original
declaration of a “crime emergency” only lasted for a month. The members of the
Guard have been deputized as specialized police by the U.S. Marshal’s Service
and issued firearms. A “summer surge” has increased the number of troops to
nearly five thousand.

The administration has now extended the deployment through the end of Trump’s
term in January 2029 even though the President’s (false) statement that the
city “has almost no crime anymore” would seem to undermine the justification
of a “crime emergency.” The nonpartisan watchdog group, Project on Government
Oversight, estimates that the deployment will eventually cost more than two
and a half billion dollars.

As Ankit Jain, one of the district’s two nonvoting U.S. Senators [told
NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/07/14/nx-s1-5892498/national-guard-deployment-
dc-2029), sending troops to a city without even notifying its elected
representatives, “you would never see that happen in any other place in the
United States of America.”

It is long past time to end the military occupation of the capital city of the
United States, yet it is hardly likely that Congress will vote to send the
troops home. The national media is giving this issue almost no attention and
the lack of congressional representation for the residents of Washington D.C.
deprives them of the voice that 50 states have.

The real solution may be to admit Washington as the 51st state. That is
something they, unlike Canadians, actually want.

The post [Free DC!](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/05/free-dc/) appeared
first on [CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
